content.text: Metals lose electrons and non-metals gain them - both arrive at a full outer shell, often the noble-gas arrangement (isoelectronic). The charges follow the group: Group 1, 2, 3 metals make 1+, 2+, 3+; Group 5, 6, 7 non-metals make 3-, 2-, 1-. The ionic bond itself is the electrostatic attraction between those opposite charges, and the formula carries no charges - the totals must cancel to zero.
